requirements.original: isvalue "(" TemplateInstance ")"
requirements.canonical: The `isvalue` operator has the syntax `isvalue "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- isvalue "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.original: The isvalue operator yields true, if the operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.
requirements.canonical: The `isvalue` operator returns `true` if its operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.

examples.text:
template charstring m_char0 := "ABCD"; //template containing a specific value matching
  template charstring m_char1 := "AB?D"; //template containing a specific value matching
                          //note, that "?" is not a matching symbol in this case
  template charstring mw_char2 := pattern "ABCD"; // a pattern matching a single value only
  template charstring mw_char3 := pattern "AB?D"; // pattern matching
  template charstring m_char4 := ("ABCD"); // template containing a specific value (expression)
  template charstring mw_char5 := ("ABCD","EFGH"); // a value list matching a single value only
  var boolean v_checkResult := isvalue(m_char0); // yields true
  v_checkResult := isvalue(m_char1); // yields true
  v_checkResult := isvalue(mw_char2); // yields false
  v_checkResult := isvalue(mw_char3); // yields false
  v_checkResult := isvalue(m_char4); // yields true
  v_checkResult := isvalue(mw_char5); // yields false

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- The isvalue operator yields true, if the operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.

requirements.original: If the operand is of record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if optional fields of the operand are set to omit.
requirements.canonical: If the operand of `isvalue` is of a record or set type, an omitted optional field SHALL be considered as initialized.
requirements.condition: the operand is of a record or set type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- If the operand is of record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if optional fields of the operand are set to omit.

requirements.original: If the operand is of record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if optional fields of the operand are set to omit.
requirements.canonical: If the operand of `isvalue` is of a record or set type, the operator SHALL also return `true` when optional fields of the operand are set to `omit` (all other fields being specific values).
requirements.condition: the operand is of a record or set type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- If the operand is of record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if optional fields of the operand are set to omit.

requirements.original: The operator shall yield false otherwise. The isvalue operator yields true, if the operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.
requirements.canonical: The `isvalue` operator SHALL return `false` if its operand is not completely initialized or does not resolve to a specific value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- The operator shall yield false otherwise. The isvalue operator yields true, if the operand is completely initialized and resolves to a specific value.

requirements.original: The specific value null is considered as concrete value.
requirements.canonical: For the `isvalue` operator, the special value `null` IS considered a specific value.

ambiguity.issue: 'concrete value' is used instead of 'specific value' used in the rest of the clause.

examples.text:
var default v_default := null;
  var boolean v_checkResult := isvalue(v_default); // yields true

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.3 -- The specific value null is considered as concrete value.

requirements.canonical: `isvalue` applied to a union alternative IS different from `ischosen`: `isvalue` checks the content of the alternative, whereas `ischosen` checks whether the alternative has been selected.

requirements.original: isbound "(" TemplateInstance ")"
requirements.canonical: The `isbound` operator has the syntax `isbound "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- isbound "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.original: The isbound operator yields true, if the operand is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The `isbound` operator returns `true` if its operand is at least partially initialized.

examples.text:
var template charstring v_char; 
  var boolean_checkResult := isbound(v_char); // yields false as v_char is uninitialized
  v_char := "AB?D";              // template containing a specific value
  checkResult := isbound(v_char);       // yields true
  v_char := pattern "AB?D";          // template containing a pattern matching
  checkResult := isbound(v_char);       // yields true

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- The isbound operator yields true, if the operand is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: If the operand is of a record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if at least one optional field of the operand is set to omit.
requirements.canonical: If the operand of `isbound` is of a record or set type, an omitted optional field SHALL be considered as initialized.
requirements.condition: the operand is of a record or set type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- If the operand is of a record or set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if at least one optional field of the operand is set to omit.

requirements.original: set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if at least one If the operand is of a record or optional field of the operand is set to omit.
requirements.canonical: If the operand of `isbound` is of a record or set type, the operator SHALL return `true` if at least one optional field of the operand is set to `omit`.
requirements.condition: the operand is of a record or set type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- set type, omitted optional fields shall be considered as initialized, i.e. the operator shall also yield true if at least one If the operand is of a record or optional field of the operand is set to omit.

requirements.original: The operator shall yield false otherwise. The isbound operator yields true, if the operand is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The `isbound` operator SHALL return `false` if its operand is not at least partially initialized.

examples.text:
var template charstring v_char; 
  var boolean_checkResult := isbound(v_char); // yields false as v_char is uninitialized
  v_char := "AB?D";              // template containing a specific value
  checkResult := isbound(v_char);       // yields true
  v_char := pattern "AB?D";          // template containing a pattern matching
  checkResult := isbound(v_char);       // yields true

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- The operator shall yield false otherwise. The isbound operator yields true, if the operand is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: Inaccessible fields (e.g. non-selected alternatives of union types, subfields of omitted record and set types or subfields of non-selected union fields) shall be considered as uninitialized, i.e. isbound shall yield for them false.
requirements.canonical: An inaccessible field (e.g. a non-selected alternative of a union, a subfield of an omitted record or set field, or a subfield of a non-selected union field) SHALL be considered as uninitialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- Inaccessible fields (e.g. non-selected alternatives of union types, subfields of omitted record and set types or subfields of non-selected union fields) shall be considered as uninitialized, i.e. isbound shall yield for them false.

requirements.original: Inaccessible fields (e.g. non-selected alternatives of union types, subfields of omitted record and set types or subfields of non-selected union fields) shall be considered as uninitialized, i.e. isbound shall yield for them false.
requirements.canonical: The `isbound` operator SHALL return `false` for an inaccessible field.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.4 -- Inaccessible fields (e.g. non-selected alternatives of union types, subfields of omitted record and set types or subfields of non-selected union fields) shall be considered as uninitialized, i.e. isbound shall yield for them false.

requirements.original: The specific value null is considered as concrete value.

requirements.original: Within expressions, fields of record and set types are referenced with the dot notation ".field".
requirements.canonical: Within an expression, a field of a record or set type IS referenced with the dot notation `.field`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.2 -- Within expressions, fields of record and set types are referenced with the dot notation ".field".

requirements.original: Elements of record of, set of, array and string types are referenced with the index notation "[index]".
requirements.canonical: An element of a `record of`, `set of`, array or string type IS referenced with the index notation `[index]`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.2 -- Elements of record of, set of, array and string types are referenced with the index notation "[index]".

requirements.original: Dot and brackets have the same binding power.
requirements.canonical: The dot `.` and the index brackets `[]` HAVE the same binding power.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.2 -- Dot and brackets have the same binding power.

requirements.original: Field references and list elements are evaluated from left to right.
requirements.canonical: Field references and list element references ARE evaluated from left to right.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.2 -- Field references and list elements are evaluated from left to right.

requirements.original: Decoded field reference is a specific notation called decoding notation that can be applied to expressions of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.
requirements.canonical: The decoding notation SHALL only be applied to expressions of type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring` or `universal charstring`.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be applied to' may be a mere capability statement or an exclusive restriction. Chosen reading: exclusive restriction, as decoding requires a string-encoded payload.
readings: The decoding notation SHALL only be applied to expressions of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.
The decoding notation CAN be applied to expressions of these string types, without excluding other types.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- Decoded field reference is a specific notation called decoding notation that can be applied to expressions of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring or universal charstring types.

requirements.original: ReferencedValue "=>" ( PredefinedType | TypeIdentifier | ( "(" Type [ "," Expression ] ")" ) )
requirements.canonical: A decoded field reference has the syntax `ReferencedValue "=>" ( PredefinedType | TypeIdentifier | ( "(" Type [ "," Expression ] ")" ) )`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- ReferencedValue "=>" ( PredefinedType | TypeIdentifier | ( "(" Type [ "," Expression ] ")" ) )

requirements.original: The ReferencedValue preceding the => symbol in a decoding notation shall be decoded into a value of the type following the => symbol.
requirements.canonical: The ReferencedValue preceding the `=>` symbol in a decoding notation SHALL be decoded into a value of the type following the `=>` symbol.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- The ReferencedValue preceding the => symbol in a decoding notation shall be decoded into a value of the type following the => symbol.

requirements.original: Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error. The ReferencedValue preceding the => symbol in a decoding notation shall be decoded into a value of the type following the => symbol.
requirements.canonical: A failure of decoding in a decoding notation SHALL cause a test case error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- Failure of this decoding shall cause a test case error. The ReferencedValue preceding the => symbol in a decoding notation shall be decoded into a value of the type following the => symbol.

requirements.original: In case the ReferencedValue is of the universal charstring type and the extended syntax with parentheses is used, the Type can be followed by an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.canonical: If the ReferencedValue is of `universal charstring` type and the extended syntax with parentheses is used, the Type MAY be followed by an optional parameter defining the encoding format.
requirements.condition: the ReferencedValue is of universal charstring type and the parenthesized syntax is used
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- In case the ReferencedValue is of the universal charstring type and the extended syntax with parentheses is used, the Type can be followed by an optional parameter defining the encoding format.

requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of a decoding notation SHALL be of `charstring` type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: The encoding format parameter of a decoding notation SHALL contain one of the strings allowed for the `decvalue_unichar` function (clause C.5.4).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: Any other value shall cause an error. The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).
requirements.canonical: An encoding format parameter value other than the strings allowed for `decvalue_unichar` SHALL cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The kind of error is not specified: a compile-time error when the value is known statically, or a runtime test case error.
readings: An invalid encoding format value SHALL cause a compile-time error if statically known, otherwise a test case error.
An invalid encoding format value SHALL always cause a runtime test case error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- Any other value shall cause an error. The parameter shall be of the charstring type and it shall contain one of the strings allowed for the decvalue_unichar function (specified in clause C.5.4).

requirements.original: In case the ReferencedValue is not a universal `charstring, the optional parameter shall not be` present.
requirements.canonical: If the ReferencedValue is not of `universal charstring` type, the encoding format parameter SHALL NOT be present.
requirements.condition: the ReferencedValue is not of universal charstring type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- In case the ReferencedValue is not a universal `charstring, the optional parameter shall not be` present.

requirements.original: a) If the type following the => symbol is not enclosed into parentheses, only a built-in type or a type reference consisting of a single identifier can be used.
requirements.canonical: If the type following the `=>` symbol is not enclosed in parentheses, it SHALL be a built-in type or a type reference consisting of a single identifier.
requirements.condition: the type following => is not parenthesized
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- a) If the type following the => symbol is not enclosed into parentheses, only a built-in type or a type reference consisting of a single identifier can be used.

requirements.original: Extended type references shall always use the extended syntax with parentheses.
requirements.canonical: An extended type reference following the `=>` symbol SHALL always use the extended syntax with parentheses.

ambiguity.issue: 'Extended type reference' is not defined; it presumably means any type reference other than a built-in type or single identifier (e.g. qualified names or field sub-type references).

improper_terms.proper: type reference not consisting of a single identifier

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.3 -- Extended type references shall always use the extended syntax with parentheses.

requirements.original: A module may refer to the TTCN-3 language version and to package versions being used.
requirements.canonical: A module MAY refer to the TTCN-3 language version and to the package versions it uses.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.0 -- A module may refer to the TTCN-3 language version and to package versions being used.

requirements.original: The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.
requirements.canonical: The transfer syntax of a TTCN-3 module SHALL be UTF-8, with each character of the module individually encoded and decoded according to UTF-8 as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.0 -- The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.

requirements.original: The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.
requirements.canonical: The encoded form of a TTCN-3 module SHALL NOT contain characters that do not correspond to any character of the module.

readings: The encoded module SHALL NOT contain any byte sequence (e.g. a byte order mark) that does not correspond to a module character.
The encoded module SHALL NOT contain invalid UTF-8 sequences; a byte order mark is tolerated.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a UTF-8 byte order mark counts as a 'character not corresponding to any character of the module'; the strict reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.0 -- The transfer syntax of TTCN-3 modules shall be UTF-8, i.e. each character of the module shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Transformation Format 8 (UTF-8) as defined in annex R of ISO/IEC 10646 [2] and no characters not corresponding to any character of the module shall be present.

requirements.canonical: A module IS defined with the keyword `module`.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 modules have an explicit import interface to use definitions from other TTCN-3 or non-TTCN-3 modules.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module has an explicit import interface to use definitions from other TTCN-3 or non-TTCN-3 modules.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- TTCN-3 modules have an explicit import interface to use definitions from other TTCN-3 or non-TTCN-3 modules.

requirements.original: It is possible to hide definitions in a TTCN-3 module (see clause 8.2.5).
requirements.canonical: A definition in a TTCN-3 module CAN be hidden from other modules by means of visibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- It is possible to hide definitions in a TTCN-3 module (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.original: They are reusable and parameterizable.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable.

readings: A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable by means of module parameters.
A TTCN-3 module IS parameterizable with formal parameters like other parameterizable objects.
ambiguity.issue: 'Parameterizable' is not explained; given clause 8.2.1 the module-parameter reading is chosen (the module syntax has no formal parameter list).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- They are reusable and parameterizable.

requirements.original: Module names are of the form of a TTCN-3 identifier.
requirements.canonical: A module name SHALL be a TTCN-3 identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- Module names are of the form of a TTCN-3 identifier.

requirements.original: In addition, a module specification can carry an optional attribute identified by the language keyword that identifies the edition of the TTCN-3 language, in which the module is specified.
requirements.canonical: A module specification MAY carry an optional attribute, introduced by the `language` keyword, that identifies the edition of the TTCN-3 language in which the module is specified.

examples.text:

requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- In addition, a module specification can carry an optional attribute identified by the language keyword that identifies the edition of the TTCN-3 language, in which the module is specified.

requirements.canonical: A language string identifying the core language edition SHALL be one of the listed strings "TTCN-3:2001" ... "TTCN-3:2023".

requirements.canonical: A module SHALL give at most one language string defining the core language version in which the module is defined.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- a) At most one language string per module shall be given to define the core language version in which the module is defined.

requirements.original: b) Per extension package, at most one extension package string of that extension package shall be used by a module.
requirements.canonical: For each extension package, a module SHALL use at most one extension package string of that extension package.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 8.1 -- b) Per extension package, at most one extension package string of that extension package shall be used by a module.
